notes.1a: Both the income statement and the statement of financial position were prepared to a high standard with many fully correct submissions. The most common errors in the income statement were the incorrect treatment of the opening and closing subscriptions balances and the omission of the irrecoverable debt. There were no common errors in the statement of financial position.
notes.1b: Nearly all candidates gave the required advice. Most candidates supported their advice with at least one valid point of justification and some gave two valid points and were rewarded with the three available marks.
notes.1c: Most candidates demonstrated their knowledge of life membership but some did not state the relevant accounting concept.
notes.2a: This was the least well answered question part on the paper and few candidates had sufficient knowledge of IAS 38 to gain any credit.
notes.2b: (i) There were many correct calculations for AB plc with no common errors. The calculations for CD plc and EF plc were less well answered with many candidates not accounting correctly for the depreciation of the product and amortisation of the patent. Some candidates did not calculate the number of shares correctly for the latter two companies and a few failed to give their answer to the nearest whole cent.
notes.2bii: The price earnings ratio calculations were well answered with many candidates being awarded three marks. A few candidates failed to give their answer to two decimal places.
notes.2c: Nearly all candidates stated two appropriate ratios.
notes.2d: Nearly all candidates provided the required advice and most justified their answer satisfactorily.
notes.2e: Most candidates provided a reasonable explanation.
notes.2f: Candidates demonstrated their knowledge of the contents of the report with a high number stating one correct matter and some stating two matters worthy of credit.
notes.3a: Many candidates suggested one appropriate reason with some providing a valid second reason.
notes.3b: The forecast income statement was very well prepared with many fully correct statements. Some candidates provided incorrect calculation of the administrative expenses.
notes.3c: The forecast capital accounts were well prepared with some fully correct accounts. Some candidates did not treat the goodwill correctly. Some candidates reversed the entries while some failed to account for the revaluation of the non-current assets.
notes.3d: Many candidates were able to state one advantage and some did state two appropriate advantages.
notes.3e: This was very well answered with nearly all candidates giving the required advice and a high number justifying their answer to a sufficiently high standard to receive three marks.
notes.4a: Although there were few candidates who were able to provide three valid reasons, there were many who gave two reasons and overall knowledge was acceptable.
notes.4b: Performance was variable ranging from a fully correct statement to a list of items not shown in the required IAS 7 format. Few candidates were able to derive the increase in trade receivables and the decrease in trade payables. Marks were often lost for placing items in the incorrect section of the statement and for not totalling and labelling the net cash from operating, investing and financing activities.
notes.5a: A high number of candidates calculated the variances correctly. The least errors were made on the sales volume variance calculation and the most errors were made on the material usage variance calculation.
notes.5b: The discussion of the changes in the variances was well answered with many candidates being awarded eight marks and no common errors.
notes.5c: Most candidates gave the required advice and the justification was generally acceptable but few candidates were awarded full marks as there was often little consideration of the down side of the decision.
notes.5d: Although most candidates stated one appropriate reason few were able to state two reasons.
notes.6a: Some candidates stated the correct term but there was also a range of incorrect answers.
notes.6b: The total profit calculations were made without errors by a very high number of candidates.
notes.6c: Likewise, the calculations were made correctly by most candidates with no common errors.
notes.6d: Few candidates suggested an appropriate base for apportionment with hardly any candidate providing two bases.
notes.6e: Most candidates gave the required advice and many justified their answer to a high standard.
notes.general_comments:
Overall candidates performance was reasonable. Questions 1 and 6 were the best answered questions on
